statements.proposition: Other popular Redis clients (ioredis, node-redis) handle backward compatibility with a similar HELLO-fallback approach.
statements.note: Rule 2 class 5: a statement about other upstream projects, not about what the author did, ran or verified in this change. Judged as not a claim about this change.
evidence: PR message sentence compares the approach to ioredis and node-redis; the change list (src/valkey/valkey.zig, test/js/valkey/*) contains nothing about those projects

statements.proposition: This change introduces no breaking changes for existing users of the Bun Redis/Valkey client.
statements.label: CANNOT_TELL
statements.note: No concrete check settles it. The diff only adds a private flag and a fallback path in src/valkey/valkey.zig; no public name is removed, renamed or re-signatured. However the fallback triggers on any HELLO error containing 'unknown command' or 'HELLO', and handleResponse changes branch order for unauthenticated state, so behaviour for existing Redis 6+ users could change in edge cases. Verifying would need building Bun (Zig) and running against Redis servers, not feasible here.
